title: When the Prom Falls
premise: Gideon Marchetti, a seventeen-year-old coder who runs an anonymous account exposing small-town secrets, has spent five years hiding his family's disgrace after his mother's disappearance. When he finds coded directions in his late grandmother's recipe box, he discovers she was documenting how the school board covered up a toxic contamination that sickened students—including, possibly, his mother. As Gideon decodes the recipes and falls for Priya, the board president's daughter who is investigating the same mystery from the other side, he must choose between staying invisible and going public. In the end, Gideon publishes everything under his real name at prom night, when the whole town is gathered, forcing the board's resignation and finally letting himself belong.
about_author: Bram Villalobos is a former high school journalism teacher who spent a decade watching teenagers ask better questions than adults dared to. He writes in a converted garage in central California, where his own grandmother's recipe box still sits on the shelf, mostly for cooking.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Account
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. We meet him posting as @hollowcreekwatch, exposing a coach's falsified attendance records while eating lunch alone in the library server room. Establishes his rules: never reveal yourself, never get attached. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness disguised as safety.

chapters.title: Five Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Flashback woven through present: his mother vanished when he was twelve, and the town whispered. His father retreated into silence; Gideon learned that attention is dangerous. A classmate invites him to prom committee; he declines. Beat: the cost of invisibility made tender.

chapters.title: Grandma's Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Clearing his grandmother's kitchen after her funeral, he finds index cards among the recipes—measurements that don't make sense, dates, initials, one card reading 'NOT FOOD.' The last card names the old east wing of Hollow Creek High. Beat: grief cracking open into dread.

chapters.title: Priya Rao, Board President's Daughter
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She's archiving school board minutes for a civics project and notices five years of redacted maintenance reports—all dated around her childhood friend Tommy's illness. She crosses paths with Gideon, who flinches from her questions. Beat: two investigators orbiting the same wound.

chapters.title: Card Seven: Simmer Slowly
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Decoding card seven as coordinates to the sealed east wing boiler room, he breaks in at night and finds corroded pipes and a faded inspection sticker predating its official install date. Someone else has been there recently—fresh boot prints. Beat: the thrill and terror of being right.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Got Sick
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She visits Tommy Delgado, now nineteen and on oxygen, who remembers the winter the east wing smelled like pennies and everyone's gums bled. His mother made him sign something. Beat: righteous anger kindling into purpose.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching the Watcher
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. His anonymous account receives a message: 'Stop digging, Marchetti.' His identity—known only to himself—is exposed. He realizes the board has someone inside the district's IT contractor. Beat: paranoia tightening; the safe distance collapses.

chapters.title: Study Hall Truce
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Gideon and Priya, each suspecting the other of leaking information, confront each other and instead compare notes over cafeteria coffee. First real conversation; first laugh in years. Beat: reluctant alliance becoming something warmer.

chapters.title: What Dad Buried in the Garage
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Searching his father's locked filing cabinet, Gideon finds his mother's old employment records—she worked as a custodian in the east wing, and her medical file ends abruptly before her disappearance. His father catches him and begs him to stop. Beat: family fracture along the fault line of truth.

chapters.title: Card Twelve Serves Six
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Card twelve decodes to a list of six names—the students who got sickest, including Tommy and, in different handwriting, his mother. Grandma knew. Grandma documented everything and hid it where only family would look. Beat: love revealed retroactively; grief recontextualized.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Sabotage
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, on prom committee, discovers the venue was quietly changed away from the school gym—the same gym built over the contaminated wing. Her father signs the change order personally. At home, she finds a shredder running past midnight. Beat: betrayal by blood.

chapters.title: The Account Goes Dark
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. His account is suspended after a coordinated report campaign; his drafts, evidence files, and the decoded cards are wiped from his cloud. Only the physical recipe box remains. He almost quits. Priya shows up at his door with printed copies she'd secretly made. Beat: despair met by unexpected loyalty.

chapters.title: Tommy's Signature
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They track down the NDA Tommy signed: it names Halcyon Environmental, a testing firm owned by the board treasurer's brother-in-law. The tests were faked; the water reports were forged. Beat: the conspiracy acquires a shape, and it's bigger than they feared.

chapters.title: Threats at the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Someone keys his father's truck and leaves a dead sparrow on the porch. His father, terrified, reveals he always suspected the truth but stayed silent to protect Gideon. Father and son argue, then grieve together. Beat: fear versus duty inside the family.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower Who Wasn't Brave
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts her father privately. He doesn't deny it—he says he was twenty-eight, outvoted, scared, and then complicit for a decade. He won't confess publicly but slips her a key to a storage unit. Beat: the banality of cowardice, and a crack of conscience.

chapters.title: Storage Unit 44
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The unit holds original water samples, lab results, and his mother's final letter—she'd found the contamination herself, reported it, was fired, and left town alive but broken, choosing exile over a fight she couldn't win. She's been sending money anonymously ever since. Beat: the mystery of the mother resolved into ache, not villainy.

chapters.title: Countdown to Prom
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Three days until prom, when the entire town will be in one building. Gideon drafts the exposé but hesitates: publishing under his real name means losing every shield he has. Priya tells him anonymity kept him safe but never alive. Beat: the decision crystallizing between them, and between them.

chapters.title: They Find the Box
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The Marchetti house is ransacked; the recipe box is gone. But Gideon anticipated this—he photographed every card weeks ago and stashed backups with Tommy's mother, the one adult who never stopped asking questions. Beat: the hunted becoming prepared; resolve hardening.

chapters.title: When the Prom Falls
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Prom night. Under the paper stars and the rented lights, Gideon takes the stage during the king and queen announcement and publishes everything live—his name attached, his face on the projector. The room goes silent, then erupts. Priya stands beside him. Beat: the climax; invisibility burned away in front of everyone.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Parking Lot
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Outside, phones buzzing, the treasurer resigning by morning news cycle, Tommy's family already calling lawyers. Gideon's father arrives—not angry, but holding his mother's number. 'She deserves to know you finished it,' he says. Beat: trembling aftermath, connection replacing armor.

chapters.title: The Call
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon calls his mother. A long silence, then her voice—older, wary, real. She tells him about the day she found the pipes; he tells her about grandma's recipe box. Neither apologizes; both begin again. Beat: reconciliation without erasure of the hurt.

chapters.title: A New Recipe
chapters.summary: Dual POV, closing. Weeks later: hearings scheduled, the east wing condemned, Tommy breathing easier after a settlement. Gideon writes his first post under his real name—a thank-you letter to the town and to the girl beside him. In the recipe box, now refilled, Priya adds a card of her own. Beat: belonging earned, love chosen, memory honored.
